title: Power series in generators of I map onto the I-adic completion
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in R$ ($n\geq0$), $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$, and $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_mR/I^m$ the $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For $F=\sum_Ea_Ex^E\in R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and $m\geq1$ put $F_{<m}(f)=\sum_{|E|<m}a_Ef^E\in R$ (with $f^E=f_1^{e_1}\cdots f_n^{e_n}$, $|E|=e_1+\cdots+e_n$). Then $\Phi(F)=(F_{<m}(f)\bmod I^m)_{m\geq1}$ is an element of $R^\wedge$, and $\Phi:R[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to R^\wedge$ is a surjective ring homomorphism with $\Phi(x_i)=(f_i\bmod I^m)_m$ and $\Phi(r)=(r\bmod I^m)_m$ for $r\in R$.

proof.text: (Generators of $I^m$.) For every $m\geq0$, $I^m$ is the ideal generated by the monomials $f^E$ with $|E|=m$; equivalently, $y\in I^m$ if and only if $y=P(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ for a polynomial $P\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ homogeneous of degree $m$. Proof by induction on $m$: $I^0=R=(f^0)$; if $I^m=(f^E:|E|=m)$ then $I^{m+1}=I^m\cdot I$ is generated by the products $f^Ef_i=f^{E+e_i}$ ($|E|=m$, $1\leq i\leq n$), and these are exactly the $f^{E'}$ with $|E'|=m+1$ (such an $E'$ has some $e'_i\geq1$, and $E'=(E'-e_i)+e_i$). An $R$-linear combination $\sum_{|E|=m}c_Ef^E$ is $P(f)$ for the homogeneous $P=\sum_{|E|=m}c_Ex^E$, and conversely. In particular $a f^E\in I^{|E|}\subseteq I^m$ for all $a\in R$ whenever $|E|\geq m$. (In Mathlib: Ideal.mem_span_pow_iff_exists_isHomogeneous, Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPolynomial/Homogeneous.lean:671.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian, line 23065), second proof, lines 23075-23084 ('well defined and surjective ring map (details omitted)'); details written out by the agent

proof.text: ($\Phi(F)\in R^\wedge$.) Let $F=\sum_Ea_Ex^E$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Each $F_{<m}(f)$ is a finite sum (there are finitely many $E\in\mathbf N^n$ with $|E|<m$), so it is an element of $R$. For $m\geq1$, $F_{<m+1}(f)-F_{<m}(f)=\sum_{|E|=m}a_Ef^E\in I^m$ by step 1. Hence the transition map $R/I^{m+1}\to R/I^m$ sends $F_{<m+1}(f)\bmod I^{m+1}$ to $F_{<m+1}(f)\bmod I^m=F_{<m}(f)\bmod I^m$, so $(F_{<m}(f)\bmod I^m)_m$ is a compatible sequence, i.e. an element of $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_mR/I^m$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] (for an index $m=0$, if the limit includes it, $R/I^0=0$ and there is nothing to check). Iterating, $F_{<m'}(f)\equiv F_{<m}(f)\bmod I^m$ for all $m'\geq m$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian, line 23065), second proof, lines 23075-23084 ('well defined and surjective ring map (details omitted)'); details written out by the agent

proof.text: ($\Phi$ is additive and has the stated values.) The ring operations of $R^\wedge$ are componentwise [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and those of $R[[x]]$ coefficientwise [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For $F=\sum a_Ex^E$, $G=\sum b_Ex^E$: $(F+G)_{<m}(f)=\sum_{|E|<m}(a_E+b_E)f^E=F_{<m}(f)+G_{<m}(f)$, so $\Phi(F+G)=\Phi(F)+\Phi(G)$. For $r\in R$ (the series $rx^0$) and $m\geq1$, $(rx^0)_{<m}(f)=r$, so $\Phi(r)=(r\bmod I^m)_m$, the image of $r$ under $R\to R^\wedge$; in particular $\Phi(1)=1$. For $x_i$: $(x_i)_{<m}(f)=f_i$ for $m\geq2$ and $(x_i)_{<1}(f)=0\equiv f_i\bmod I$ since $f_i\in I$; so $\Phi(x_i)=(f_i\bmod I^m)_m$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian, line 23065), second proof, lines 23075-23084 ('well defined and surjective ring map (details omitted)'); details written out by the agent

proof.text: ($\Phi$ is multiplicative.) With $F=\sum a_Ex^E$, $G=\sum b_{E'}x^{E'}$ we have $FG=\sum_D(\sum_{E+E'=D}a_Eb_{E'})x^D$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $f^{E+E'}=f^Ef^{E'}$, $|E+E'|=|E|+|E'|$. Hence $(FG)_{<m}(f)=\sum_{|E|+|E'|<m}a_Eb_{E'}f^Ef^{E'}$ while $F_{<m}(f)G_{<m}(f)=\sum_{|E|<m,\,|E'|<m}a_Eb_{E'}f^Ef^{E'}$. Every pair in the first sum occurs in the second, so $F_{<m}(f)G_{<m}(f)-(FG)_{<m}(f)=\sum a_Eb_{E'}f^{E+E'}$ over the finitely many pairs with $|E|<m$, $|E'|<m$, $|E|+|E'|\geq m$; each term lies in $I^{|E+E'|}\subseteq I^m$ by step 1. So $(FG)_{<m}(f)\equiv F_{<m}(f)G_{<m}(f)\bmod I^m$ for every $m$, i.e. $\Phi(FG)=\Phi(F)\Phi(G)$ componentwise in $R^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. With step 3, $\Phi$ is a ring homomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian, line 23065), second proof, lines 23075-23084 ('well defined and surjective ring map (details omitted)'); details written out by the agent

proof.text: ($\Phi$ is surjective.) Let $\xi\in R^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]: $\xi=(\bar r_m)_{m\geq1}$ with $\bar r_m\in R/I^m$ compatible; choose lifts $r_m\in R$ of $\bar r_m$. Compatibility means $r_{m+1}-r_m\in I^m$ for $m\geq1$. By step 1 choose for each $m\geq1$ a polynomial $P_m\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ homogeneous of degree $m$ with $P_m(f)=r_{m+1}-r_m$, and put $P_0=r_1$ (homogeneous of degree $0$). Since the $P_m$ are homogeneous of pairwise distinct degrees, $F=\sum_{m\geq0}P_m$ is a well-defined power series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]: its coefficient $a_E$ is the coefficient of $x^E$ in $P_{|E|}$. Then for $m\geq1$, $\sum_{|E|<m}a_Ex^E=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}P_k$, so $F_{<m}(f)=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}P_k(f)=r_1+\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}(r_{k+1}-r_k)=r_m$ (telescoping). Hence $\Phi(F)=(r_m\bmod I^m)_m=\xi$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_surjective_toAdicCompletion {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R) (I : Ideal R) (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f)) : ∃ Φ : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) R →+* AdicCompletion I R, (∀ (F : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) R) (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → AdicCompletion.evalₐ I m (Φ F) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ m) (MvPolynomial.eval f (MvPowerSeries.truncTotal m F))) ∧ Function.Surjective Φ ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, Φ (MvPowerSeries.X i) = AdicCompletion.of I R (f i)) ∧ (∀ r : R, Φ (MvPowerSeries.C r) = AdicCompletion.of I R r)
